question: Can one robust planar homography fitted to the unchanged SC34 coherent-cycle component repair the failed affine extent transport without changing identity support or either negative decision?

predecessor.failure_attribution: SC34 retained 0.442978 primary cycle opportunity and 0.981006 dominant-component support, while both cross-scene negatives had zero cycles. The affine transported extent reached only 0.065238 target bbox IoU.

projective_model.input: All unchanged correspondences in the largest 8-connected coherent-cycle component.
projective_model.threshold_origin: Reuse the frozen six-pixel maximum cycle-error scale as the single MAGSAC reprojection scale; no numeric sweep.
projective_model.extent: Project the four corners of the already-bound reference extent through the homography; query truth remains evaluation-only.

literature_motivation.used_principle: RoMa supplies robust dense correspondences under viewpoint change; MAGSAC++ robustly estimates homographies from contaminated correspondences. A planar projective model can express perspective that an affine envelope cannot.

evaluation.negative_decisions: Inherit the two zero-cycle non-commits unchanged from the predecessor; do not rerun or reinterpret them.

forbidden_after_freeze: change the model family, six-pixel scale, majority, cycle, direct-exit or extent threshold
crop, rectify, add query truth, select correspondences by target IoU or retry another estimator
claim a consumed one-positive mechanism repair is fresh confirmation
claim_boundary: This is one consumed SC34 posthoc Development intervention that changes only affine extent extrapolation to a robust projective homography. A pass can show mechanism plausibility on this failure and no more. It remains same-provider, privileged-reference, desktop-model evidence and does not establish arbitrary repeated-door identity, raw-camera initial binding, named entrance, ownership, access, traversability, waypoint, arrival, handoff, deployment, user benefit, reliability or safety.
